extra.message: User-controlled 'host' query parameter (GET parameter) is directly concatenated into an os.system() call without any sanitization. An attacker can inject shell metacharacters (e.g., ?s=8.8.8.8;cat+/etc/passwd) to execute arbitrary OS commands with server privileges.

The 'copyline' query parameter from user input is directly concatenated into an HTML string and returned via HTMLResponse at line 24 without any escaping or sanitization. This allows reflected XSS attacks where a crafted URL can execute arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser.

The 'card' query parameter (GET parameter with default 'pending') is rendered through Jinja2 Template with the '|safe' filter at line 81, which explicitly bypasses auto-escaping. Combined with HTMLResponse return, this allows stored/reflected XSS where an attacker can inject arbitrary HTML/JavaScript.

The 'name' query parameter is directly used as a file path at line 139: BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name without traversal validation. An attacker can supply '../' sequences in the filename to write files outside the intended directory (e.g., name=../../../etc/cron.d/malicious). No input sanitization or whitelist is applied.

The 'ref' query parameter is used at line 60 to construct a file path: BASE_EXPORT_DIR / f'{ref}.json' without any validation against directory traversal. Combined with writing arbitrary JSON data at line 62, an attacker could write files to unintended locations.

The lxml XML parser at line 147 is configured with resolve_entities=True and no_network=False. This means external entities defined in the XML document (passed via request body) will be resolved by the server. An attacker can craft a malicious XML payload to read arbitrary files on the server (e.g., !ENTITY x system 'file:///etc/passwd') or trigger SSRF attacks, even with no_network=False as local DTD resolution still occurs.

The /ops/vault/seller-stash-247 endpoint writes and serves hardcoded PII including a Social Security Number (ssn: '111-22-3333') and credit card number (card: '4111111111111111') in response data. These are not masked or encrypted, violating PCI-DSS and privacy regulations. The endpoint also accepts user-controlled ssn/card values to persist to disk.

The /ops/wire/seller-tally-226 endpoint logs the full request body and Authorization header at line 52 using logger.warning. This exposes potentially sensitive data (API keys, credentials) to log files, which may be accessible to other processes or systems. No redaction is performed before logging.

The /ops/origin/seller-mirror-667 endpoint takes the Origin request header and sets it directly as Access-Control-Allow-Origin with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials=true at line 97-98. This allows any external origin to make authenticated cross-origin requests, enabling credential theft via malicious websites.

extra.message: Default DATABASE_URL contains hardcoded credentials: postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/marketplace. Anyone with access to the source code can directly connect to the database using these credentials.

SECRET_KEY for JWT token generation has a default value of 'your-secret-key-change-in-production'. If this is used in production without overriding via .env or environment variable, anyone can forge valid authentication tokens by signing their own JWT with this known secret.

CORS middleware at line 20 sets allow_origins to specific localhost URLs but allow_credentials=True combined with allow_headers=['*'] is overly permissive. While not as severe as the seller_operations SSRF issue, this combination in production would allow any origin to make authenticated cross-origin requests.

The 'host' parameter has a default value of '127.0.0.1' but accepts user input at line 116-118. The parameter is used in os.system() ping command, enabling remote code execution via shell injection. Note: This endpoint lacks the _wrk_gate token check (gate_ref depends on it) due to Python's argument evaluation order - gate_ref is validated after host parameter parsing.

The /ops/nonce/seller-roll-707 endpoint uses Python's 'random' module (non-cryptographic PRNG) to generate security codes at lines 124-125. The 'random' module is not suitable for cryptographic purposes as its output can be predicted by observing a portion of the generated sequence.

extra.message: The /ops/digest/seller-fold-284 endpoint uses MD5 for hashing at line 70. MD5 is cryptographically broken and vulnerable to collision attacks. While the primary usage here may not be security-critical, using MD5 in any authentication-related context is unsafe.

The /ops/mongo/seller-lane-717 endpoint accepts a 'filter' parameter from the request JSON body at line 132 and passes it directly to MongoDB's find_one() query method. An attacker can inject NoSQL operators (e.g., {'$gt': ''}) to bypass authentication queries or extract arbitrary data from any collection in the database.

The /ops/frame/seller-slip-677 endpoint sets X-XSS-Protection header to '0' (disabling browser XSS filter) and Content-Security-Policy to empty string at lines 105-106. These security headers are anti-patterns that disable built-in browser protections.

The login endpoint at line 54 stores the JWT token in an HTTP-only cookie as 'access_token'. However, the authentication check in dependencies.py line 20-24 shows that tokens can be passed via either Authorization header or cookies. Combined with CORS configuration, this dual-pass mechanism for transmitting sensitive auth tokens increases the attack surface.
